accepted.s: Which one of the following Greek envoys was sent by Antiochus I of Syria to the court of Bindusara?
accepted.x: Deimachus was sent by Antiochus I of Syria to the court of Bindusara.
accepted.tq: Use the envoy–sender–ruler relationship rather than recalling the name alone.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Dionysius, who visited the Mauryan court, was sent by:
accepted.x: Dionysius was sent by Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt to the court of Bindusara.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely associated foreign envoys by their sending rulers.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Megasthenes' Indica is available to historians mainly through quotations preserved by which of the following authors?
accepted.x: The original Indica has not survived; it is known through quotations by Strabo, Arrian and Diodorus.
accepted.tq: Identify the surviving form of a lost literary source through its principal transmitters.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Megasthenes described the society of India as divided into how many classes?
accepted.x: Megasthenes divided Indian society into seven classes, including philosophers, farmers, soldiers and councillors.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical figure associated with a classical account.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the seven classes described by Megasthenes?
accepted.x: Megasthenes listed philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, artisans, soldiers, overseers and councillors. Merchants were not included in this seven-class description.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider by comparing every option with the complete named list.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In Megasthenes' account, the philosophers of India comprised:
accepted.x: Megasthenes identified Brahmanas and Sramanas, or ascetics, as philosophers.
accepted.tq: Test a subcategory within a larger descriptive classification.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Palibothra:
1. Palibothra has been identified with Pataliputra.
2. It was situated at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers.
3. It was protected by a wooden wall.
4. It had 64 gates and 570 towers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe Palibothra, the Greek designation of Pataliputra.
accepted.tq: Check whether the geographical, structural and numerical details all belong to the same city.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The municipal administration of Palibothra, according to Megasthenes, was conducted by:
o: A 40-member body divided into four boards
A 30-member body divided into six boards
A council of 12 members divided into three boards
A council of 64 members divided into eight boards
accepted.x: Megasthenes described a 30-member municipal body organised into six boards at Palibothra.
accepted.tq: Separate the exact institutional composition from nearby city statistics.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Megasthenes' account from the evidence of Mauryan sources?
o: Megasthenes claimed there were no slaves in India, although slavery existed according to the Arthashastra and Ashokan edicts.
Megasthenes reported slavery, whereas Mauryan sources denied it.
Megasthenes discussed only slavery and not Indian society.
Both Megasthenes and the Arthashastra denied the existence of slavery.
accepted.x: Megasthenes claimed that India had no slaves, but the Arthashastra and Ashokan edicts indicate that slavery did exist.
accepted.tq: Resolve a contradiction between a foreign observation and indigenous evidence.
accepted.sec: Foreign envoys and Indica's descriptions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which literary source is primarily associated with administration, economy, espionage and taxation?
accepted.x: Kautilya's Arthashastra deals with administration, economy, espionage and taxation.
accepted.tq: Match a work with its central subject rather than its author alone.
accepted.sec: Literary sources - author and subject  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who wrote the Mudrarakshasa?
accepted.x: Vishakhadatta wrote the Mudrarakshasa, which describes the overthrow of the Nandas and the rise of Chandragupta.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–work association while avoiding ruler–work substitution.
accepted.sec: Literary sources - author and subject  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Source)
A. Mahavamsa and Dipavamsa
B. Divyavadana and Ashokavadana
C. Parishishtaparvan
D. Puranas

List-II (Subject)
1. Legends of Ashoka
2. Genealogies of Mauryan kings
3. Chandragupta's Jain end
4. Ashoka's conversion and spread of Buddhism to Lanka

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Mahavamsa and Dipavamsa concern Ashoka and Buddhism in Lanka; Divyavadana and Ashokavadana contain Ashokan legends; Parishishtaparvan describes Chandragupta's Jain end; the Puranas give genealogies.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure source–subject pair and eliminate incompatible codes.
accepted.sec: Literary sources - author and subject  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Parishishtaparvan is attributed to Hemachandra and deals with Chandragupta's Jain end.
accepted.tq: Detect the swapped author–work combinations.
accepted.sec: Literary sources - author and subject  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following works is associated with the legend of Chanakya dating to the tenth century?
accepted.x: Vamsatthapakasini is associated with a tenth-century Chanakya legend.
accepted.tq: Identify the less familiar source by its distinctive subject and period.
accepted.sec: Literary sources - author and subject  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The account of the southern expansion of the Mauryas is associated with which Tamil author?
accepted.x: Mamulanar, a Tamil author, is associated with references to the southern expansion of the Mauryas.
accepted.tq: Link a regional literary reference with its author.
accepted.sec: Literary sources - author and subject  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: James Prinsep deciphered the inscriptions of Ashoka in:
accepted.x: James Prinsep first deciphered the Ashokan inscriptions in 1837.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year attached to a landmark discovery.
accepted.sec: Literary sources - author and subject  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Chandragupta Maurya assumed the Magadhan throne in 321 BC after overthrowing:
accepted.x: Chandragupta Maurya took the Magadhan throne in 321 BC from Dhana Nanda, with the assistance of Chanakya.
accepted.tq: Connect a ruler with the predecessor he displaced.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following names refer to the same adviser of Chandragupta Maurya?
1. Chanakya
2. Kautilya
3. Vishnugupta
4. Parvataka
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Chanakya was also known as Kautilya and Vishnugupta. Parvataka was a Himalayan chief who allied with Chandragupta, not another name for Chanakya.
accepted.tq: Separate alternative names from the name of an allied political figure.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Greek name used for Chandragupta Maurya was:
accepted.x: Greek sources referred to Chandragupta Maurya as Sandrocottus.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Greek form of a ruler's name from titles of Ashoka.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement best represents the difference among traditions regarding the origin of the Mauryas?
o: All Brahmanical, Buddhist and Jain sources describe Chandragupta as a Brahmana.
Buddhist sources link Maurya to Mura, while Brahmanical sources identify a Moriya Kshatriya clan.
Brahmanical sources link Maurya to the Shudra woman Mura, whereas Buddhist and Jain sources describe Chandragupta as a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.
All traditions identify Chandragupta as a foreign ruler from Syria.
accepted.x: Brahmanical sources connect the name Maurya with Mura, while Buddhist and Jain traditions identify Chandragupta with the Kshatriya Moriya clan.
accepted.tq: Compare conflicting source traditions without merging their claims.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following territories was NOT ceded by Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya under their treaty?
accepted.x: The treaty involved Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae and Aria. Bactria is not included in the listed cessions.
accepted.tq: Compare every territorial option with the complete treaty list.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the result of the treaty between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus Nicator?
o: The treaty ended all diplomatic contact between the Mauryas and the Seleucids.
Chandragupta surrendered Magadha and accepted Seleucus as his suzerain.
Chandragupta received territories in the northwest, while Seleucus received 500 elephants and entered into a marriage alliance.
Seleucus received 500 elephants and Chandragupta received no territory.
accepted.x: Seleucus ceded northwestern territories to Chandragupta, while receiving 500 elephants and concluding a marriage alliance.
accepted.tq: Combine the territorial, military and diplomatic outcomes of a treaty.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Chandragupta's treaty with Seleucus Nicator
B. Chandragupta's accession to the Magadhan throne
C. Repair of Sudarshana lake by Rudradaman I
D. Chandragupta's death at Shravanabelagola
accepted.x: Chandragupta became ruler in 321 BC, defeated Seleucus in 305 BC, later died at Shravanabelagola, and Sudarshana lake was repaired by Rudradaman I much later.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest political events first and place the later inscriptional event last.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Sudarshana lake at Girnar in Saurashtra was originally constructed by:
accepted.x: Pushyagupta Vaishya, the governor of Chandragupta Maurya, constructed Sudarshana lake.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original builder from later canal-makers and repairers.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Sudarshana lake is correct?
o: It was built at Pataliputra by Chanakya and repaired by Seleucus.
It was built at Taxila by Megasthenes for Chandragupta.
It was built by Rudradaman and later destroyed by Skandagupta.
It was built at Girnar by Pushyagupta and later had canals added by Tushaspha.
accepted.x: Sudarshana lake was built by Pushyagupta at Girnar; Ashoka's Yavanaraja Tushaspha later added canals. Rudradaman I and Skandagupta were later associated with repairs.
accepted.tq: Use the builder–location–later intervention combination to reject swapped details.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the description of Chandragupta Maurya's army, its approximate strength included:
accepted.x: The army is described as having approximately 600,000 infantry and 30,000 cavalry.
accepted.tq: Keep the two numerical components in their correct order and category.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who described Chandragupta Maurya's army as a 'gang of dacoits'?
accepted.x: The Roman historian Justin used the expression 'gang of dacoits' for Chandragupta's army.
accepted.tq: Match a distinctive quotation with its correct author.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly describes the final phase of Chandragupta Maurya's life?
o: He became a disciple of Bhadrabahu, abdicated during a famine, went to Shravanabelagola and died by Sallekhana.
He adopted Buddhism, conquered Kalinga and died at Pataliputra.
He became an Ajivika, retired to Taxila and died in battle.
He became a disciple of Upagupta, abdicated after the Kalinga War and died at Ujjain.
accepted.x: Chandragupta became a disciple of Bhadrabahu, abdicated during a 12-year famine, went to Shravanabelagola and died by Sallekhana.
accepted.tq: Arrange the linked biographical stages rather than selecting an isolated name.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta Maurya - rise, Kautilya, Seleucus, Sudarshana, Jain end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of Ashokan titles and meanings is correctly matched?
o: Devanampiya — conqueror of Kalinga; Piyadasi — lord of Magadha
Devanampiya — king of Ujjain; Piyadasi — protector of Taxila
Devanampiya — teacher of Dharma; Piyadasi — enemy of the Greeks
Devanampiya — beloved of the gods; Piyadasi — of pleasing looks
accepted.x: Ashoka used Devanampiya in the sense of beloved of the gods and Piyadasi in the sense of of pleasing looks.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar royal epithets by their exact meanings.
accepted.sec: Ashoka - titles, viceroyalties, accession  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In which two minor rock edicts does the personal name 'Ashoka' occur?
accepted.x: The name Ashoka appears in the Maski and Gujarra minor rock edicts.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific inscriptional locations of a personal name.
accepted.sec: Ashoka - titles, viceroyalties, accession  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Before becoming emperor, Ashoka served as viceroy of which of the following places?
accepted.x: Ashoka served as governor of Taxila and as viceroy of Ujjain before his accession.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a prince's viceroyalty from the later provincial capitals of the empire.
accepted.sec: Ashoka - titles, viceroyalties, accession  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka's succession:
1. Ashoka was the son of Bindusara and Subhadrangi.
2. He faced a succession struggle with Susima.
3. He acceded approximately in 273/272 BCE.
4. His coronation took place approximately in 269 BCE.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe Ashoka's parentage, succession struggle, accession and coronation.
accepted.tq: Verify the sequence of parentage, succession, accession and coronation.
accepted.sec: Ashoka - titles, viceroyalties, accession  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement about the tradition that Ashoka killed 99 brothers is most accurate?
o: It is accepted as a precise historical census of the royal family.
It is regarded as an exaggeration, while Rock Edict V refers to the families of his brothers.
It refers only to the sons of Bindusara's ministers.
It is mentioned in Rock Edict XIII as the cause of the Kalinga War.
accepted.x: The Mahavamsa's account of 99 brothers is considered exaggerated; Rock Edict V refers to the families of Ashoka's brothers.
accepted.tq: Separate a legendary numerical claim from the more limited inscriptional evidence.
accepted.sec: Ashoka - titles, viceroyalties, accession  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Kalinga War took place in approximately 261 BCE and marked which year of Ashoka's reign?
accepted.x: The Kalinga War occurred in the eighth year of Ashoka's reign, around 261 BCE, and became a turning point in his life.
accepted.tq: Pair the event with both its regnal year and approximate absolute date.
accepted.sec: Ashoka - titles, viceroyalties, accession  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Samprati — Ajivika patron of Nagarjuni caves
accepted.x: Bindusara is associated with Ajivika beliefs. Dasharatha patronised the Ajivikas, while Samprati is associated with Jainism.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–religion table to identify the correctly matched pair.
accepted.sec: Religion followed by Mauryan rulers  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which Mauryan ruler is described as the 'Ashoka of Jainism'?
accepted.x: Samprati is known as the 'Ashoka of Jainism' and is associated with Jainism.
accepted.tq: Identify a ruler through a distinctive religious epithet.
accepted.sec: Religion followed by Mauryan rulers  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement about the Barabar caves is correct?
o: They are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves, cut in granite, in Bihar.
They are located at Girnar and were constructed by Rudradaman.
They were excavated at Shravanabelagola for Jain monks by Chandragupta.
They are the latest surviving brick caves, built in Bengal, for Buddhists.
accepted.x: The Barabar caves in Bihar are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves and are carved in granite.
accepted.tq: Combine monument, material, location and superlative details.
accepted.sec: Religion followed by Mauryan rulers  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the southern extent of the Mauryan Empire:
1. Brahmagiri contains a minor edict of Ashoka.
2. Siddapura and Jatinga-Rameshwara also mark the southern reach.
3. The Tamil kingdoms of Chola, Pandya, Satyaputra and Keralaputra lay outside the empire.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Mauryan southern reach extended to parts of Karnataka, while the listed Tamil kingdoms remained outside it.
accepted.tq: Test geographical limits through evidence sites and excluded neighbouring kingdoms.
accepted.sec: Extent - southern limits and Andhra  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following places in present-day Andhra Pradesh is associated with both major and minor edicts of Ashoka?
accepted.x: Yerragudi contains both major and minor edicts of Ashoka. Rajula Mandagiri is associated with a minor edict.
accepted.tq: Distinguish two nearby inscription sites by the type of edict found there.
accepted.sec: Extent - southern limits and Andhra  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Rajula Mandagiri, associated with Ashokan evidence, is located in which district?
accepted.x: Rajula Mandagiri is a minor-edict site in Kurnool district.
accepted.tq: Link an archaeological site with its administrative location.
accepted.sec: Extent - southern limits and Andhra  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras among the peoples who:
o: Ruled the Mauryan capital at Pataliputra
Followed Ashoka's Dhamma within his domain
Served as Greek envoys at Bindusara's court
Defeated Ashoka in the Kalinga War
accepted.x: Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras among peoples following Ashoka's Dhamma within his domain; the edict is dated approximately to 256 BCE.
accepted.tq: Identify the action associated with a named people in an inscription.
accepted.sec: Extent - southern limits and Andhra  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the early relationship between the Satavahanas and the Mauryas?
o: The Satavahanas ruled only in Afghanistan as Seleucid governors.
The Satavahanas destroyed the Mauryan Empire during Chandragupta's reign.
The Satavahanas began as Mauryan feudatories and the Andhras were already Buddhist by the time of Rock Edict XIII.
The Satavahanas adopted Buddhism only after the Gupta period.
accepted.x: The Satavahanas began as Mauryan feudatories, and the Andhras are described as already Buddhist by the time of Rock Edict XIII.
accepted.tq: Combine a political relationship with a contemporaneous religious reference.
accepted.sec: Extent - southern limits and Andhra  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The province of Kalinga, added to the Mauryan Empire by Ashoka, had which capital?
accepted.x: Tosali was the provincial capital of Kalinga after its incorporation under Ashoka.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the added province from the original four provincial divisions.

accepted.s: Mauryan provinces were generally administered by:
accepted.x: The provinces were administered by princes known as Kumaras or by governors.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative authority rather than the provincial capital.
